newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end up on higher Chicago.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end up on higher Chicago.

text.p: All months of Tokyo corn futures closed higher on Friday, reflecting the CBOT corn market's price gains overnight, local traders said.
Prices were 120 to 240 yen higher, with the benchmark November 1997 up 240 yen at 14,270 yen per tonne.
All months gained from the opening, as individual investors actively bought, traders said. "Technical buying emerged throughout the day," a brokerage house trader said.
On Thursday, the yen-based corn market fell due to the yen's gains against the dollar. The yen/dollar rate will be a key factor in the market for a while, traders said.
The spot December contract on the CBOT Project A corn trading system was being traded at $2.64-3/4 per bushel at 0655 GMT, against $2.64-1/2 at Thursday's close.
The spot November of the CBOT soybean futures on the Project A overnight trading system was at $6.86-1/2 at 0655 GMT, against $6.86-1/2 at Thursday's close.
